validity.researcher_notes: The line is real, but this row duplicates P1480. Both describe the Kyiv to Western Border system with a 1020 mm first string (1970) and a 1220 mm second string. The Ukrtransgaz chronology gives 183.6 km plus 216.3 km, which is 399.9 km. The 1,112 km on this row looks like the Soviet design institute figures for two different lines added together: 522 km for Shebelinka to Dykanka to Kyiv (P1454) and 590 km for Kyiv to Western Ukraine. Ukrainian Wikipedia gives 367 km plus 506 km. No source supports 1,112 km.

verifications.note: Interfax-Ukraine, 21 September 2020: the 1020 mm Kyiv - Western Ukraine high-pressure line near Chabany was repaired and works in normal mode. Names the line as 'Київ - Західна Україна'.

fills.researcher_notes: An Interfax-Ukraine report from September 2020 says the 1020 mm Kyiv to Western Ukraine line ruptured near Chabany and was back in normal operation within days. The page uses the local name Kyiv - Western Ukraine, not the exact sheet name. This is the newest dated evidence found. No source dated 2024 or later that names this line was found, so the tier is medium.
Both pages describe a natural gas trunk line. The Interfax-Ukraine page calls it a high-pressure gas pipeline. The Ukrainian Wikipedia article covers the same system.

fills.researcher_notes: The Ukrtransgaz chronology and Ukrainian Wikipedia both date the first string to 1970. This row is the same system as P1480, so the first string year applies.

No source states 1112 km for this line. The figure looks like two separate lines added together: the Soviet design institute table lists 522 km for Shebelinka to Dykanka to Kyiv and 590 km for Kyiv to Western Ukraine, and 522 plus 590 is 1,112. The Shebelinka to Dykanka to Kyiv line is its own row, P1454. The Ukrtransgaz chronology gives 183.6 km plus 216.3 km, which is 399.9 km, on P1480. Ukrainian Wikipedia gives 367 km plus 506 km. Nothing was staged as the sheet value is not supported. See the validity record.

The Ukrtransgaz chronology and Ukrainian Wikipedia both give 1020 mm and 1220 mm for the two strings of the Kyiv to Western Border system. The Wikipedia article cites the chronology, so the two are not fully independent.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: The newest dated evidence found is a September 2020 report that the 1020 mm line was repaired and back in normal mode. No source dated 2024 or later that names this line was found, in Ukrainian or English searches, and the regulator's 2025 to 2034 plan documents checked do not mention it. The sheet status is kept. This is a weak confirm. The line is inside Ukraine west of Kyiv and may carry domestic and storage flows now that Russian transit has ended, but no source says so.
